featured_reviews.name: Rutesh Ajgaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a pleasant overall experience with good food, attentive service, and a nice ambience.
The bombil fry (4/5) stood out—fresh, crispy, and really enjoyable.

The prawns tingi (5/5) was the highlight of the meal, a must-try dish packed with great flavor.

The pomfret tawa fry (2/5) was a bit disappointing due to its small size and average taste.

Chicken tikka masala (3/5) had well-cooked chicken, but the gravy didn’t quite meet expectations.

The neer dosa (1/5) was the weakest dish—they clearly need to improve their preparation here.

Overall, a mixed experience with some excellent dishes and a few that need improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Jondhale
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Malhar recently for lunch and ordered a variety of dishes, including Crab Lollipop, Prawns Koliwada, White Rice, Rava Bombil, and Agri-style Chicken Curry. We had also planned to try Amboli and Bhakri, but unfortunately, both were out of stock.

The Crab Lollipop and Prawns Koliwada were flavorful and well-prepared. However, the Agri-style Chicken Curry did not meet expectations. The use of garam masala was overpowering, and the excessive black pepper (kalimiri) affected the overall taste, though the dish was still edible.

The ambience of the restaurant was very beautiful, but I noticed some issues with cleanliness. For example, one of the glasses provided still had food particles stuck on the edge where a person drinks. I requested the steward to replace the glass; he took the dirty one but forgot to bring a new glass altogether, leaving me to drink directly from the bottle.

While the food was average overall, I was particularly disappointed with the service. Both the steward and the captain seemed uninterested and inattentive. Despite repeated requests, it took them over 15 minutes to bring tissues, even when asked clearly and politely.

Additionally, the Prawns Koliwada was served nearly 40 minutes later, after we had almost finished our main course. At that time, only 3–4 tables were occupied in the restaurant, so such a delay was unjustified. When I raised this issue with the captain, his casual response was, "Humare yaha thoda late hi hota hai." This type of attitude is not expected from a reputed establishment like Malhar.

In summary, although the ambience was nice and some dishes were good, the poor service, lack of attention to cleanliness, and indifferent staff attitude significantly impacted our overall dining experience.

customer_updates.name: Raj Kumar Gautam (Captain)
customer_updates.text: The vendors were friendly and knowledgeable, often sharing tips on how to keep flowers fresh or suggesting combinations for floral arrangements. One vendor, an elderly woman, patiently explained how she sources her jasmine from local farms and strings them into garlands by hand. Her warmth made the experience feel personal and authentic. Prices were reasonable—₹50 for a string of jasmine, ₹100 for a kilo of marigolds, though bargaining is a must. I managed to get a beautiful mixed bouquet for ₹200 after some light negotiation.

featured_reviews.name: Shounak Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Dadar Flower Market offers a rich selection of flowers and plants in a vibrant and bustling atmosphere. It's a must-visit for flower enthusiasts and provides an authentic experience of Mumbai's market culture.

The prices at the Dadar Flower Market are generally reasonable and competitive. Since it's a wholesale market, you can expect better deals when purchasing in larger quantities. Bargaining is also common here, so don't hesitate to negotiate the prices with the vendors, especially if you're buying in bulk.

Make sure to reach here before 7 am to get fresh flowers.

featured_reviews.name: Google Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text: Dadar Flower Market is Mumbai's largest and most vibrant flower market, bursting with color and fragrance. Located near Dadar Station, this bustling market comes alive early in the morning as vendors sell a vast variety of fresh flowers, from marigolds to roses. The lively atmosphere, combined with the sight of flowers being sold in bulk, makes it a photographer's delight and a must-visit spot for anyone looking to experience the local culture.

featured_reviews.name: Danish Ansari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food Review: A Major Disappointment
​I truly believe one shouldn't speak ill of food, but I had an absolutely terrible experience here.
​We ordered the Prawns Koliwada and Crispy Chicken. Given the massive hype surrounding this restaurant, we expected the food to be exceptional. As a seafood lover—especially prawns fry—I was genuinely shocked from the very first bite. The Prawns Koliwada was completely tasteless; the spice profile was missing and there was no salt at all.
​To make matters worse, when my wife cut into a prawn, we realized they hadn't been cleaned properly. The digestive tracks (veins) were still inside. Every single prawn was like that, which completely ruined our appetite. On top of that, the dish was incredibly expensive.

​The Crispy Chicken
​The second dish was just as bad. It was so sour that after just one bite, we had to ask the waiter to pack it up. Neither my wife nor my kids could eat it—it was a total waste of money. I’ve had Crispy Chicken at many places, but this was the worst. Honestly, the local Chinese joint in my neighborhood makes it better.

​The Lesson Learned
​This experience taught me one thing: don't just rush to a restaurant based on an influencer's video. You have to check real reviews first. I have no idea what people actually like about the food there. My wife and I are beyond disappointed.

featured_reviews.name: Sawrub Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
*1/5 — Extremely disappointing*

I ordered the Chicken Dum Biryani and unfortunately it was the worst biryani I’ve had.

What went wrong:
- Taste: Bland and lacked the rich, aromatic flavor you expect from biryani. The masala tasted undercooked and oily.
-Chicken: Pieces were dry and chewy, almost rubbery. Felt like it was reheated.
-Rice: Overcooked and clumped together. No fragrance of saffron, kewra, or whole spices. -Overall quality: Greasy, heavy, and left an unpleasant aftertaste.

Value: Not worth the price at all. For what they charge, you expect proper dum-cooked biryani with tender chicken, but this missed on every count.

Would not recommend and won’t order again. If you’re craving biryani, better to skip this one.
